exposure: Caesarean section, leading to complications requiring referral
cohort: The cohort consisted of 114 women, with a mean age of 25.6 years, who were referred to a tertiary care hospital due to post-Caesarean section complications.
finding: Obstetrical complications, particularly post-partum hemorrhage (57.89%) and puerperal sepsis (20.18%), were the major causes for referral in post-Caesarean section patients, with a maternal mortality rate of 11.4%.
mod_finding: The study found that obstetrical complications, such as post-partum hemorrhage and puerperal sepsis, were the predominant reasons for referral in patients following a Caesarean section.
